author: Housnia Shams
title: Russian minister's chilling North Korea visit sends alarming warning - NewsBreak
text: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is set to visit North Korea this week, as the two countries continue to strengthen their ties amid Russia's war in Ukraine. Lavrov will begin the three-day visit on Friday, North Korea's Korean Central News Agency reported. It comes after top Kremlin security official, Sergei Shoigu, met with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Pyongyang last month. After the visit, Shoigu said Kim decided to send 5,000 military construction workers to help rebuild Russia's Kursk region. In April, Russian President Vladimir Putin thanked North Korean soldiers fighting alongside his forces in Ukraine, describing them as "heroes." It marked his first acknowledgement of the troop deployment, which Russia and North Korea had previously refused to confirm. South Korea, the US and Ukraine have said that between 10,000-12,000 North Korean troops have been deployed to the Kursk border region since last November, where Ukrainian forces launched an incursion in August. North Korea said it sent soldiers under a mutual defense pact signed with Russia last June. Pyongyang's Central Military Commission said the troops were sent to "annihilate and wipe out the Ukrainian neo-Nazi occupiers and liberate the Kursk area in cooperation with the Russian armed forces." Kim said that a monument would be erected in Pyongyang to honor fallen soldiers. In March, South Korea said that around 4,000 North Korean soldiers had been killed or wounded in the war. The deployment marks North Korea's first participation in a large-scale conflict since the end of the Korean War and an opportunity for its inexperienced military to gain modern battlefield experience. In January, South Korea and the European Union expressed concerns that Russia could reward North Korea for its troop dispatch with transfers of sensitive technology to enhance its nuclear and missile programs.
